prompt: With trustProxy set to a number (a hop count), request.ip is undefined when the socket's remoteAddress is undefined or null (as happens behind IISNode on Windows). Fix it so a missing socket address still counts as the first hop: with trustProxy: 1, an X-Forwarded-For of '2.2.2.2, 1.1.1.1' and socket.remoteAddress undefined, request.ip must be '1.1.1.1'; the same with socket.remoteAddress null. With socket.remoteAddress undefined and an X-Forwarded-Host of 'fastify.test', request.host must be 'fastify.test'.
requirement: When trustProxy is a number n, the trust function trusts hop i whenever i < n, regardless of whether the address is undefined or null. So with trustProxy: 1 and a missing socket address, the socket hop is trusted and request.ip is the last X-Forwarded-For entry ('2.2.2.2, 1.1.1.1' gives '1.1.1.1') for remoteAddress undefined and for null. With remoteAddress undefined, request.host comes from X-Forwarded-Host.

the same with socket.remoteAddress null: request.ip is '1.1.1.1'
trustProxy: 1, socket.remoteAddress undefined, X-Forwarded-Host 'fastify.test': request.host is 'fastify.test'
